name: Entrepreneur Visa (Visado de Emprendedor)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a favourable report from ENISA (Empresa Nacional de Innovación) confirming the business activity is innovative and/or of special economic interest for Spain — assessed on innovative character, scalability, founder profile, and business-plan solidity.
requirements.fix_path: Develop a business plan with concrete market analysis and financing, and submit for the preceptive ENISA report.

evidence_required.document: Business plan with market analysis and financing details
ENISA favourable report (requested ex officio by UGE-CE, issued within 10 business days once requested)

outcome.duration_length: 1-year consular visa if applying from abroad; direct 3-year authorization if already legally in Spain

sources.title: BOE — Ley 14/2013, de apoyo a los emprendedores, Art. 70 (ENISA report requirement)

notes: No fixed minimum investment — assessed via the ENISA report rather than a capital threshold, similar in spirit to Portugal's D2 case-by-case viability review and Germany's Gewerbetreibende economic-interest test, but with a genuinely distinctive feature: the ENISA report is REQUESTED EX OFFICIO by UGE-CE rather than something the applicant separately obtains and submits — a real procedural difference worth surfacing. Top rejection reasons per ENISA's own published criteria: generic financing without concrete detail, and business plans lacking real market analysis — useful, actionable fix_path-style information that most competitor sites don't surface. Genuine process advantage for in-country applicants: skipping the 1-year consular-visa stage entirely and going straight to a 3-year authorization if already legally resident — a materially faster path than the equivalent situation in most other countries in this dataset. Beckham-style tax regime (see es_dnv) is also available to entrepreneur-route holders, not re-stated here to avoid duplication.
